claims.text: The proposed material is a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy, exemplified as WxTaTiVCr.
The baseline alloy has a homogeneous microstructure with minimal pre-existing nanoprecipitates.
A stepwise heat treatment or spark plasma sintering process can introduce a controlled density of coherent TiC nanoprecipitates.
In situ TEM or synchrotron XRD can verify that only coherent nanoprecipitates form and that no unintended secondary phases are present.
The introduced coherent TiC nanoprecipitates will be reliably distributed in grain interiors and at grain boundaries.
The controlled comparison will use tensile testing near 800 °C at identical strain rates for precipitate-enriched and minimal-precipitate samples.
Coherent TiC nanoprecipitates hinder continuous dislocation glide by acting as barriers.
Coherent TiC nanoprecipitates facilitate controlled, stepwise dislocation transfer.
The combined obstruction and transfer of dislocations reduces localized stress concentrations and strain localization.
Coherent nanoprecipitates delay crack initiation by avoiding damaging dislocation pile-ups or interfacial microcracking.
At approximately 800 °C, the TiC-nanoprecipitate-enriched alloy will have greater plastic strain to failure than the baseline.
At approximately 800 °C, the TiC-nanoprecipitate-enriched alloy will have greater toughness than the baseline.
The enriched alloy will exhibit a more uniform dislocation distribution.
The enriched alloy will exhibit fewer localized-strain regions and fewer premature microcracks.
The hypothesis applies to fusion plasma-facing service conditions near 800 °C and service-representative strain rates.
The hypothesis is limited to alloys and processing routes in which coherent precipitates can be formed and maintained.
Precipitation processing may also create incoherent phases or alter grain boundaries, preventing complete isolation of the TiC effect.
The hypothesis is falsified if precipitate-enriched samples show no statistically significant improvement in both plastic strain and toughness relative to the baseline.
The presence of unintended secondary phases or incoherent precipitates would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention states that characterization will ensure the absence of unintended phases, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that such phases may still arise. The falsification rule then treats their presence as falsification, although it would instead make the experiment confounded and unable to test the TiC mechanism decisively.
